reason: The contradiction is real: at the 6/17 kickoff Joyce asked to migrate historical data (sign-ups in Phase 1), and Kobi said migration was in this phase. On 7/28 Waleed (Jumpr) called the historical migration a go-live blocker. The WAGR-370 title (from the SOW) says sign-up data was agreed. These conflict with the WAGR-470 line 'agreed scope mostly excludes them'. No later meeting decided otherwise. On 9/28 the client asked urgently for Sign-Up import templates (L3226). But Jira already tracks the open decision. WAGR-470 is an open Decision ticket for the PM. WAGR-477 (9/28, active Sprint 2) carries 'Historical Sign-Ups — yes or no' and plans an alignment doc for Emily to review. Thus the remaining gap is the wrong premise in WAGR-470 and the unchecked SOW wording, not an untracked scope gap. So severity goes down from High to Medium.

q2: Supports, with nuance. Kickoff: Joyce says 'there needs to be a step where we actually migrate all of our historical data' and asks for sign-up data in Phase 1. Kobi answers 'I did include data migration in this phase um at least for the objects that we go live with', and adds that on T&M they can load later-phase tables too. Kobi did not say 'historical' himself, but he answered a question about historical data. Sign-Up is a Phase 1 go-live object. 7/28: Joyce asks whether the CMS/API work takes priority 'over the historical data'. Waleed answers that both are 'go live blockers' and that 'the data migration is also necessary for your reps to be there and see it from day one'. He then gives the API priority for that week only. 8/11: Joyce says 'I do think we should import historical signup data'. Kobi did not call it out of scope. He said 'ultimately it's up to you' and offered a phased approach ('start with anything that's active... work backwards on the historical data afterwards'). Joyce said 'Sure'/'Yeah', but nothing was formally decided. In the same 8/11 call Kobi called only the secondary-referrer sign-up-count logic 'not currently in scope', not the migration. No transcript shows Jumpr telling the client that historical sign-ups are excluded.
q3: No later reversal. Later ledger items: L2454 (9/9 internal) says only that a historical import may happen at go-live, with no decision. L2452 (9/9 internal) is a build choice: the 253 flow will not handle backdated historical imports, because the import is expected to be a one-time event. This implies Jumpr still expected a historical import. L3226/L3227 (9/28): Emily calls Sign-Up/Referral/Player import templates urgent; no commitment was made. L2994 (9/24) is a general 'log feedback as cards' rule. The WAGR-370 closure cites a 9/24 sync, but the ledger has no 9/24 decision on historical migration scope. Later evidence makes the client expectation stronger, not weaker.
q4: Partly covered. WAGR-470 (Open, Kobi, 0 comments, Work Type Decision, epic WAGR-19) already tracks the decision on historical Sign-Ups yes or no. WAGR-477 (Open, Kobi, High, active WAG Sprint 2, created 9/28 by Taryn) repeats 'Historical Sign-Ups — yes or no' as open. It calls Sign-Up, Referral, Secondary Referral and Player 'key objects already scoped' and plans an alignment doc for Emily. WAGR-370 (Cancelled/Won't Do, unassigned, 1 comment) has the description 'Out of scope for Phase 1 (per SOW)' for migration 'beyond agreed sign-up + reference data'. That implies sign-up migration was agreed, and it contradicts the WAGR-470 premise. WAGR-20 (BUILD-07 migration plan, Ready, unassigned) covers only Agency-side rates/links transforms. No ticket records the kickoff position or corrects the WAGR-470 premise. JQL 'project = WAGR AND (text ~ historical OR text ~ migration)' returned WAGR-470, WAGR-477, WAGR-370, WAGR-20 (via epic), WAGR-124, WAGR-509 and others; none covers the variance.
